articles_applied: XXI (discovery evidence is not search activity)
constitution_recertification.key_principle: Article XXI.2: Zero results is not novelty. Article XXVIII: Each promotion requires new evidence. The retraction below applies Article XXVIII in reverse — a claim that was promoted without sufficient evidence must be demoted.

retraction.why_retracted: The CEO audit identified 2026 literature that directly overlaps the proposed classifier territory. The Round 56g prior-art search was INCOMPLETE — it searched for papers using specific query strings but did not find the 2026 nationwide and phenotype-stratified studies that explicitly address phenotype-based VSS risk stratification.

corrected_classification.BROAD_PHENOTYPE_BASED_VSS_RISK_STRATIFIC: EXISTING — explicitly established by Lakhani 2026 (n=1,497) and Maroufi 2026 (4-phenotype comparative effectiveness)
corrected_classification.EXACT_R2_C3_PREDICTION: NOT ESTABLISHED — no study distinguishes R2-C3 from other failure phenotypes
corrected_classification.PATENT_PRIOR_ART: INCONCLUSIVE — 6 patent searches found no direct hits, but the patent landscape was not exhaustively searched (Article XXI.2: zero results ≠ novelty)

lesson_per_article_xxxi.the_lesson: A prior-art search that returns zero results does NOT mean the territory is untouched. It means the specific query strings did not match. The 2026 studies use different terminology ('symptom phenotypes', 'individualized risk stratification') that my Round 56g queries did not capture.
lesson_per_article_xxxi.the_failed_assumption: I assumed that searching for 'headache phenotype + VSS selection' would find any prior art on phenotype-based VSS selection. This was wrong — the 2026 studies use 'symptom phenotypes' and 'presenting symptoms' rather than 'headache phenotype (ICHD-3)'.
lesson_per_article_xxxi.the_affected_artifacts: Round 56g ROUND56G_HYPOTHESIS_ATTACK_AND_WEAK_LABELS.json — the prior_art_attack section claims survival. This is corrected in Round 56h.
lesson_per_article_xxxi.the_tests_added: Future prior-art searches must use MULTIPLE terminology variants (symptom phenotype, presenting symptom, headache-only, phenotype-stratified, individualized risk stratification, etc.) and must search BOTH literature AND patents.

study_1_Lakhani_2026.title: Symptom Phenotypes and Treatment Failure of Dural Venous Sinus Stenting in Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension: A Nationwide Analysis
study_1_Lakhani_2026.outcome: IIH-related inpatient readmission within 300 days (9.6%); repeat intervention (6.5%)
study_1_Lakhani_2026.key_finding: Headache-only → HR 8.35 for readmission (p=0.002) vs visual-only (2.6%). Visual+other and mixed/nonvisual also elevated (HR 4.25, 4.50).
study_1_Lakhani_2026.explicit_conclusion: 'These findings underscore the importance of individualized risk stratification and symptom-specific counseling when selecting patients for VSS.'
what_this_ESTABLISHES: Presenting symptom phenotype (coarse categories) predicts VSS failure (readmission)
Headache-only presentation is the HIGHEST-RISK phenotype
The concept of phenotype-based VSS patient selection is EXPLICITLY endorsed
what_this_does_NOT_establish: Does NOT predict the TYPE of failure (R2-C1 vs R2-C2 vs R2-C3 vs R2-C4 vs R2-C5)
Does NOT use ICHD-3 headache classification (uses coarse 'headache-only' category)
Does NOT use physiological measurements (ICP, gradient, venous distribution) as predictors
Does NOT use CGRP or other biomarkers
Does NOT identify the R2-C3 subgroup specifically (headache despite normal ICP + improved papilledema + no restenosis)
Does NOT distinguish R2-C3 from R2-C1 (both would present as 'headache-only' and both would lead to readmission)

study_2_Maroufi_2026.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Venous Sinus Stenting and Ventricular Shunting for IIH: A Phenotype-Stratified, Propensity-Matched Cohort Study
study_2_Maroufi_2026.outcome: Persistent headache, papilledema, visual disturbance at 24 months; retreatment, ED visits
study_2_Maroufi_2026.key_finding: VSS preferable in nonobese-no-visual; VS (shunt) better papilledema control in obese-no-visual. Both similar efficacy with baseline visual impairment.
study_2_Maroufi_2026.explicit_conclusion: 'The comparative effectiveness of VSS and VS in IIH varies by phenotype... These findings underscore the need for phenotype-guided, prospective trials.'
what_this_ESTABLISHES: Obesity × visual phenotype → comparative effectiveness of VSS vs shunt
The concept of phenotype-guided treatment selection is EXPLICITLY endorsed
what_this_does_NOT_establish: Does NOT predict failure TYPE within a treatment arm (only compares arms)
Does NOT use ICHD-3, CGRP, or venous manometry
Does NOT distinguish R2-C3 from R2-C1 within the headache outcome

cumulative_2026_evidence.broad_phenotype_based_VSS_risk_stratific: ESTABLISHED — Lakhani 2026 (symptom phenotype → readmission) + Maroufi 2026 (obesity×visual phenotype → comparative effectiveness)
cumulative_2026_evidence.exact_R2_C3_prediction: NOT ESTABLISHED — neither study distinguishes R2-C3 from other failure phenotypes
cumulative_2026_evidence.physiological_trajectory_prediction: NOT ESTABLISHED — neither study uses ICP, gradient, or venous distribution as predictors
cumulative_2026_evidence.failure_TYPE_prediction: NOT ESTABLISHED — both studies predict BINARY outcomes (readmission yes/no, headache yes/no), not WHICH failure phenotype

old_target_RETIRED.description: Pre-treatment headache phenotype classifier for VSS response (success/failure)
old_target_RETIRED.why_retired: The broad territory of phenotype-based VSS risk stratification is EXPLICITLY established by Lakhani 2026 and Maroufi 2026. A classifier that merely reproduces 'headache-only → high risk' would NOT be an invention — it would replicate existing findings.
old_target_RETIRED.what_the_2026_literature_already_does: Lakhani 2026: symptom phenotype → readmission risk (HR 8.35). Maroufi 2026: obesity×visual phenotype → comparative treatment effectiveness. The 2026 literature already supports symptom-phenotype-based VSS risk stratification.

narrowed_target.description: Pre-treatment phenotype + physiological trajectory → specific FAILURE-TYPE prediction (R2-C1 vs R2-C2 vs R2-C3 vs R2-C4 vs R2-C5) → different treatment pathway
what_makes_this_different_from_2026_lite: Lakhani 2026 predicts BINARY readmission (yes/no). The narrowed target predicts WHICH failure phenotype.
Maroufi 2026 compares treatment ARMS (VSS vs shunt). The narrowed target predicts WITHIN-ARM failure type.
Neither 2026 study uses PHYSIOLOGICAL measurements (ICP, gradient, venous distribution). The narrowed target ADDS physiological trajectory to phenotype.
Neither 2026 study distinguishes R2-C3 from R2-C1. The narrowed target specifically identifies R2-C3 (headache despite normal ICP + improved papilledema + no restenosis).
narrowed_target.the_key_question: Can we predict the TYPE of failure, not merely the probability of readmission or retreatment?
narrowed_target.why_this_might_be_the_real_gap: The 2026 literature shows that phenotype matters (headache-only = high risk). But it does NOT tell us WHY headache-only patients fail. Do they fail because of: (a) R2-C1 (persistent ICP elevation), (b) R2-C2 (restenosis), (c) R2-C3 (pressure-independent headache), (d) R2-C4 (visual failure), or (e) R2-C5 (other)? Without knowing WHICH failure type, the clinician cannot choose the right alternative treatment. A classifier that predicts failure TYPE would enable phenotype-SPECIFIC treatment pathways.
narrowed_target.commercial_value_if_demonstrated: HIGH — a 'failure-type prediction' tool would change the clinical decision from 'should we stent?' (already being addressed by 2026 literature) to 'IF this patient fails, HOW will they fail?' (not addressed by any existing system). Different failure types require different salvage treatments: R2-C1 → CSF shunt; R2-C2 → re-stenting; R2-C3 → CGRP antagonist / migraine prophylaxis; R2-C4 → optic nerve sheath fenestration; R2-C5 → symptomatic management.
narrowed_target.classification: DISCOVERY HYPOTHESIS — NOT promoted. Per Article XXVIII, this is a hypothesis that requires evidence, model, validation, and conclusion before any invention claim.

does_the_narrowed_target_add_value_beyon.question: If headache-only already predicts outcome strongly (Lakhani HR 8.35), does a fancy classifier that predicts failure-TYPE add value?
does_the_narrowed_target_add_value_beyon.answer: UNKNOWN — cannot be tested at zero cost. The 2026 studies do not report failure-type data, only binary outcomes. To test whether failure-type prediction adds value over binary prediction, we would need per-patient failure-type labels in a cohort that also has the predictors. No such open dataset exists.
does_the_narrowed_target_add_value_beyon.strongest_alternative_article_xxxii: The alternative explanation is that headache-only patients fail for a SINGLE dominant reason (e.g., all R2-C1, or all R2-C3), in which case failure-type prediction adds NO value over binary prediction. If headache-only patients are HETEROGENEOUS in failure type, then failure-type prediction adds value. We cannot distinguish these alternatives without per-patient failure-type data.
